messages.subject: filterByCoverage dummy question
parts:
Hello Altuna,

First many thanks for developping MethylKit. It's a fantastic R package, very useful.

So I have a very dummy question that I think I have the answer to but want to double check as I did not find the answer in the manual or in other questions in this google group.

I have a 'MethRaw' object with 6 samples. I read everything with a minimum coverage of 1 to look at the distribution of coverage and % methylation.

Then when I am using the following command what am I doing:

filterByCoverage(methRaw,lo.count=X, lo.perc=NULL, hi.count=Y,hi.perc=NULL)

i think I am removing all cytosines that overall (=accross all samples) have a coverage (=number of overlapping read) < X and > Y.

So if reads are distributed evenly between samples and I want to filter out everything with a coverage bellow 10 and above 100 in each samples I need to set X=10*6 and Y=100*6 ?

Many thanks for you help,

Romain

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] filterByCoverage dummy question
parts:
Hi Romain,
This is a sample specific cutoff, if you want to retain bases with at least 10X and at most 100X coverage in any given sample you just need to set lo.count=10, hi.count=100

no need to multiply.

Best,

altuna
